title: 21 electrodes of International 10-20 system
teaching_note: Electrode map; locations are distinct from a montage of channel pairs. SVG is original source drawing.

title: Human EEG with prominent alpha rhythm
teaching_note: Real human resting EEG; posterior 11-Hz rhythm and corresponding spectral peak. Source does not specify participant age or eyes-open transition.

title: cEEGrid eyes-open to eyes-closed alpha
credit: Bleichner MG and Debener S (2017). Concealed, Unobtrusive Ear-Centered EEG Acquisition: cEEGrids for Transparent EEG. Front Hum Neurosci 11:163. doi:10.3389/fnhum.2017.00163
specific_credit: Martin G. Bleichner and Stefan Debener
teaching_note: Recorded ear-EEG, not standard 10-20 scalp montage. Five seconds; alpha amplitude increases on eye closure.

title: Adult sleep theta, K-complex and slow-wave sleep
credit: Bleichner MG and Debener S (2017). Concealed, Unobtrusive Ear-Centered EEG Acquisition: cEEGrids for Transparent EEG. Front Hum Neurosci 11:163. doi:10.3389/fnhum.2017.00163
specific_credit: Martin G. Bleichner and Stefan Debener
teaching_note: Actual overnight recording from author Stefan Debener. Ear-EEG channels plus EOG, ECG and motion; do not label as a standard scalp montage or a spindle-specific figure.

title: Pediatric asynchronous sleep spindles
credit: Britton JW et al.; St. Louis EK and Frey LC (eds). Electroencephalography (EEG): An Introductory Text and Atlas. American Epilepsy Society, 2016.
specific_credit: Elia M. Pestana-Knight, MD, Cleveland Clinic Foundation
teaching_note: 16-month-old boy; a documented example, not a claim that every spindle asymmetry is benign.

title: Trace alternant in neonatal quiet sleep
credit: Britton JW et al.; St. Louis EK and Frey LC (eds). Electroencephalography (EEG): An Introductory Text and Atlas. American Epilepsy Society, 2016.
specific_credit: Elia M. Pestana-Knight, MD, Cleveland Clinic Foundation
teaching_note: Quiet sleep in a 25-day-old girl born at 39 weeks; interpret discontinuity with age and behavioral state.

title: Delta brushes in premature infant
credit: Britton JW et al.; St. Louis EK and Frey LC (eds). Electroencephalography (EEG): An Introductory Text and Atlas. American Epilepsy Society, 2016.
specific_credit: Elia M. Pestana-Knight, MD, Cleveland Clinic Foundation
teaching_note: 32-week conceptional-age infant in sleep; delta with superimposed fast activity is a developmental graphoelement.

title: Pediatric posterior dominant rhythm
credit: Britton JW et al.; St. Louis EK and Frey LC (eds). Electroencephalography (EEG): An Introductory Text and Atlas. American Epilepsy Society, 2016.
specific_credit: Elia M. Pestana-Knight, MD, Cleveland Clinic Foundation
teaching_note: 11-month-old infant with 5–6 Hz PDR; adult frequency expectations cannot be applied directly.

title: Eye flutter artifact
credit: Britton JW et al.; St. Louis EK and Frey LC (eds). Electroencephalography (EEG): An Introductory Text and Atlas. American Epilepsy Society, 2016.
teaching_note: Anterior and frontopolar prominence helps distinguish an ocular origin.

title: Electrode pop artifact
credit: Britton JW et al.; St. Louis EK and Frey LC (eds). Electroencephalography (EEG): An Introductory Text and Atlas. American Epilepsy Society, 2016.
teaching_note: F3 electrode pop; a sharp-looking transient need not be epileptiform.
